title: "Stable MCI extended DMP scatter"
subtitle: "Effect size correlation across a series of p value cutoffs"
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false
#| cache: false

pacman::p_load(rstatix, ggtext, colorspace, geomtextpath, install = FALSE)

# Prefer all dplyr functions
conflicted::conflict_prefer_all("dplyr", quiet = TRUE)
```

## Introduction

Show the correlation between the stable_mci effect size and the effect sizes of the other dementia categories at a series of p value cutoffs. Display the difference between the two groups of CG sites.

## Load the data

### Association data

Read the association data filtered to the CG sites with nlog10_p_value >= 5, and split the sites into the main and outlier groups on the stable_mci effect size.

```{r}
stable_mci_es_cutoff <- -0.2

asso <-
  read_rds(here("data/publicly_available/association_nlog10_p_value_lgeq5_wide.rds")) |>
  mutate(stable_mci_grp = if_else(estimate_stable_mci < stable_mci_es_cutoff, "outlier", "main"))

glimpse(asso)
```

## Function for selecting cg sites

```{r}
source(here("custom_func/select_sig_cg.R"))

# Test the function
select_sig_cg(asso, 6) |>
  glimpse()
```

## Collect data by p value cutoff

Select effect size for p value cutoff 5:7, assemble the data into a long format tibble.

```{r}
effect_size_series <-
  5:7 |>
  set_names() |>
  map(~ select_sig_cg(asso, .x)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "pval_cutoff") |>
  # Remove the nlog10_p_value columns
  select(-starts_with("nlog10_p_value_")) |>
  # Remove "estimate_" from the column names
  rename_all(~ str_remove(.x, "^estimate_"))

glimpse(effect_size_series)
```

## Make a data preparation function

This function accepts a data tibble, filters out the outliers, annotates `pval_cutoff` with the site count, and computes the correlation between stable_mci and a second dementia category. *P* values are labelled by the shared Spearman label helper in the manuscript's house style (three significant figures, a decimal at *P* ≥ 0.01 and scientific notation below; custom_func/p_value_label.R). It never prints 0: it re-runs the test with the t approximation when the default returns 0, and prints "P < 1.0 x 10^-300" only for true underflow.

```{r}
#| output: false

source(here("custom_func/display_scientific_notation.R"))
source(here("custom_func/spearman_p_label.R"))
source(here("custom_func/r_value_label.R"))

# Plotmath labels (parsed by geom_text), so exponents print as superscripts as in Figure 1

effect_size_for_scatter_plot <- function(.data, filter_condition = TRUE, demcat2 = normal2incid) {
  .data |>
    # Filter out the outliers
    filter({{filter_condition}}) |>
    # Count the number of cg sites
    add_count(pval_cutoff, name = "n_cg") |>
    # Modify pval_cutoff
    mutate(
      pval_cutoff = glue(
        "{pval_cutoff} <br><span style = 'font-size:6pt'> (n={format(n_cg, big.mark = \",\")}) </span>"
      )
    ) |>
    # Calculate the correlation between two dementia categories and create a label
    mutate(
      .by = c(pval_cutoff, stable_mci_grp),
      cor = cor.test(stable_mci, {{demcat2}}, method = "spearman")$estimate,
      # Never 0 unless the value underflows (R1.5/R2.7)
      cor_pval = spearman_p_value(stable_mci, {{demcat2}}),
      # The group name leads the label, which is printed in a panel corner rather than along the line
      cor_label = glue(
        '"{stable_mci_grp}:"~{r_value_label(cor)}*";"~{spearman_p_label(cor_pval)}'
      )
    )
}

# Test the function
effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition = between(prev, -1.4, 0.3),
    demcat2 = prev
  ) |>
  glimpse()
```

## Make a plotting function

This function accepts a data tibble and plots a scatter plot of the effect size of stable_mci against a second dementia category, faceted by p value cutoff.

The correlation labels sit in the bottom-left corner of each panel, one line per group, as in the other effect-size scatter figures. Written along the regression line, the main-group labels ran past the panel edge and were clipped once the *P* values were printed in full (R1.5); the bottom-left corner is empty, or holds at most two corner points, in every panel.

```{r}
#| output: false

make_effect_size_scatter_plot <- function(.data, demcat2 = "prev", ...) {
  .data |>
    ggplot(aes(x = stable_mci, y = .data[[demcat2]], colour = stable_mci_grp)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1,
      key_glyph = draw_key_point
    ) +
    # One label per panel and group, main above outlier
    geom_text(
      data = \(d) d |>
        distinct(pval_cutoff, stable_mci_grp, cor, cor_pval, cor_label) |>
        mutate(label_y = if_else(stable_mci_grp == "main", 0.165, 0.09)),
      aes(y = I(label_y), label = cor_label),
      x = I(0.07),
      hjust = 0,
      size = 6 / .pt,
      colour = "black",
      parse = TRUE,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_color_discrete_qualitative(palette = "Dark 3") +
    # Show a gray dashed line at x = 0 and y = 0
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    facet_wrap(~ pval_cutoff, scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
    # Axis titles say "effect size" (= ΔM, the covariate-adjusted M-value difference from stable
    # normal, defined in the legend; R2.7). The authors preferred "effect size" to "ΔM" (2026-10-09).
    labs(
      x = "stable_mci effect size",
      y = glue(
        "{dc} effect size",
        dc = if (demcat2 == "prev") "Prevalent dementia" else glue("{demcat2} transition")
      )
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Stable MCI Group", theme(legend.title.position = "left"))) +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_textbox_simple(halign = 0.5, lineheight = 0.1, margin = margin(8, 2, 2, 2)),
      legend.position = "top"
    )
}
```

## Initialize a list for storing the plots

```{r}
scatter_list <- list()
```

## Prev vs stable_mci

```{r}
#| label: fig-prev
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

scatter_list$prev <-
  effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(
    filter_condition = between(prev, -1.4, 0.3),
    demcat2 = prev
  ) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat2 = "prev")

scatter_list$prev
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-normal2incid

scatter_list$normal2incid <-
  effect_size_series |>
  effect_size_for_scatter_plot(demcat2 = normal2incid) |>
  make_effect_size_scatter_plot(demcat2 = "normal2incid")

scatter_list$normal2incid
```
